# Piecewise Linear Mapping and Integration

Also called: Piecewise Linear Transfer Function Integration

## Overview
This family encompasses techniques that approximate the volume rendering integral or opacity mapping using piecewise linear functions to enable analytical solutions or efficient hardware acceleration. It differs from [Linear Opacity Interpolation](7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md) by supporting more complex mappings (such as gradient scaling or density reparameterization) and from [SDF-based Opacity Derivation via Logistic CDF](3233-sdf-based-opacity-derivation-via-logistic-cdf.md) by relying on explicit linear approximations rather than probabilistic cumulative distribution functions.

## Shared principles
The family operates on the scalar field $V(\mathbf{p})$ sampled at positions $\mathbf{p}$ along the ray [S2, 2789, unofficial]. The core mechanism involves a transfer function $T$ that maps the scalar value to a color vector $\mathbf{c} \in [0,1]^3$ and an opacity scalar $\alpha \in [0,1]$ [S2, 2789, unofficial]. These values are subsequently used in the front-to-back compositing equation defined in [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) [S2, 2789, unofficial]. Transfer functions are typically parameterized by control points $(V_k, \mathbf{c}_k, \alpha_k)$ with interpolation between points [S2, 2789, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Piecewise Density Approximation for Reparameterized Sampling](1139-piecewise-density-approximation-for-reparameterized-sampling.md)
This method approximates the optical density field $\sigma_r(t)$ along a ray as either piecewise constant or piecewise linear on a fixed grid, enabling the analytical computation of the cumulative opacity integral [1139-piecewise-density-approximation-for-reparameterized-sampling]. By inverting the resulting monotonic cumulative opacity function, it generates volume samples that are uniformly distributed in opacity space rather than Euclidean space [1139-piecewise-density-approximation-for-reparameterized-sampling]. It sets itself apart from [Piecewise Linear Mapping and Integration](9000-piecewise-linear-mapping-and-integration.md) by explicitly constructing a piecewise approximation of the *density* to facilitate closed-form inversion.

### [Piecewise Linear Opacity Mapping with Gradient Scaling](1335-piecewise-linear-opacity-mapping-with-gradient-scaling.md)
This method maps scalar volume values to opacity using piecewise linear functions defined by tissue types, then scales the resulting opacity by the magnitude of the local gradient vector to suppress tissue interiors and enhance bounding surfaces [1335-piecewise-linear-opacity-mapping-with-gradient-scaling]. It addresses the limitation of binary classification by ensuring all voxels map to non-zero opacity, rendering thin regions as faint wisps [1335-piecewise-linear-opacity-mapping-with-gradient-scaling]. It sets itself apart from [Linear Opacity Interpolation](7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md) by explicitly incorporating gradient magnitude to modulate opacity based on local data variation.

### [Linear Opacity Interpolation](7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md)
Linear Opacity Interpolation maps scalar volume data values to opacity using linear interpolation between two threshold values [7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md]. It solves the problem of isolating objects of interest by assigning high opacity to grey values inside the object and low or zero opacity to surrounding values [7016-linear-opacity-interpolation.md]. It sets itself apart from its siblings by using simple linear interpolation between two thresholds, whereas [Piecewise Linear Opacity Mapping with Gradient Scaling](1335-piecewise-linear-opacity-mapping-with-gradient-scaling.md) incorporates gradient information.

### Power Function Opacity Transfer
- **Definition**: A simple power function used to map voxel values to opacity before enhancement, allowing illustrative enhancements to supplement existing volume rendering mechanisms [S1].
- **Step**: Calculate the gradient used for enhancement from the dataset *after* the simple power function transfer function has been applied, as this gradient is more effective in capturing subtle features [S1].
- **Formula**: $o_v = (k_{os}v_i)^{k_{oe}}$, where $v_i$ is the volume sample value, $k_{os}$ is the scalar controlling maximum opacity, and $k_{oe}$ is the exponent [S1].
- **Parameters**: $k_{os}$ controls maximum opacity; $k_{oe}$ controls contrast ($<1$ softens differences, $>1$ increases contrast) [S1].

### Piecewise Linear Transfer Function Integration
- **Definition**: A rendering technique that integrates piecewise linear transfer functions using a 2D texture map to compute correct exponential per-pixel opacity [S2, unofficial].
- **Parameter**: Texture Map: A 2D texture map parameterized by opacity and thickness [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The concept of integrating piecewise linear transfer functions using hardware-accelerated texture maps was described in the context of GPU-based volume rendering of unstructured grids [S2, unofficial]. The use of power functions for opacity transfer to enhance subtle features in volume illustration was introduced by Rheingans [S1].

## Sources
[S1] Volume illustration: nonphotorealistic rendering of volume models, https://www.csee.umbc.edu/~rheingan/pubs/volillus.tvcg01.pdf, fetched 2026-10-27
